paragraphs: Upgrade the high-load anaerobic digestion and relieve acid stress through the strategy of side-stream micro-aeration: biochemical performances, microbial response and intrinsic mechanisms
Wen Lia, Yongli Liua, Baocun Wua, Li Gua*, Rui Dengb

Key laboratory of the Three Gorges Reservoir Region’s Eco-environments, Ministry of Education, Institute of Environment and Ecology, Chongqing University, 174 Shapingba Road, Chongqing, 400045, P.R. China

OLR 5.0 gVS/L·d, before and after the introduction of micro-aeration
Table S2b Operational conditions for different stages in micro-aeration participated groups

Table S2a describes the experimental design and analysis of the three groups of reactors. First, three groups of reactors were used as controls for structures and micro-aeration to explore the role of micro-aeration in the side-stream reactor. In addition, enzymes, C-blance, CLSM, microbial and microbial and metagenomic analysis were performed before and after the introduction of micro-aeration to further explore the intrinsic mechanisms of SMA.

Table S2b describes the operational conditions for different stages in micro-aeration participated groups, with OLR gradually increasing from 2.5 to 5.5 g VS/L, while changing the micro-aeration situation at the OLR of 5.0 g VS/L. The analysis of the effect of micro-aeration on the system focused on the OLR of 5.0 g VS/L.
Figure S1 Schematic diagram of the device structure

Sludge run in a single-stage reactor to acidification was transferred to four reactors under an organic load of 5.0 g VS/L. R1, R2, R3, R4 and side-stream reactors have the same structure with the effective volume of 0.7 L. Different doses of micro-aeration (5, 10, 20 and 30 mL/d) were applied in these four reactors respectively and their operational performance is shown in Figure S2. The results in direct micro-aeration with different gas dosage give us the right dosage in SMA research, and 20 mL/d was selected as the optimal dose.
